title: Canonical shifts of module derived functors and pullback compositors
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For a scheme $T$, let $R_T$ be its pullback from the point [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and let $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T})$ be the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. For every scheme morphism $u:S\to T$, use the specified total derived functors $P_u=Lu^*:D_T\to D_S$ and $G_u=Ru_*:D_S\to D_T$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], computed on K-flat and K-injective resolutions respectively. Write $D(u^*)$ for termwise exact pullback followed by localization, and let $c_u:P_u\xrightarrow{\sim}D(u^*)$ be its canonical comparison [def-sfb-left-derived-exact]. Give $D(u^*)$ the termwise integer shifts, $P_u$ the shifts transported along $c_u$, and $G_u$ its fixed K-injective shifts. These $P_u$ and $G_u$ are exact functors, and $c_u$ agrees with the comparison obtained by shifting the K-flat resolutions, for every integer shift.
For composable $S\xrightarrow{u}T\xrightarrow{v}U$, let $b_{u,v}:(vu)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u^*v^*$ be the ordinary module pullback compositor [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] and let $m_{u,v}:P_{vu}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_uP_v$ be the specified derived compositor of [prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp]. Under $c_{vu},c_u,c_v$ and the canonical termwise derived composition identification, $m_{u,v}$ is the localized termwise map $b_{u,v}$; its degree-$r$ representative on $M[n]$ is $b_{u,v,M^{r+n}}$. The compositor and its inverse commute with all the specified integer shifts.
For any commutative square $p:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, $p':X'\to Y'$ with $gp'=pg'$, let $\theta:P_{p'}P_g\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{g'}P_p$ be $m_{p',g}^{-1}$ followed by the identification $P_{gp'}=P_{pg'}$ and $m_{g',p}$. For every $K\in D_Y$ and every integer $n$, $s^n_{P_{g'}P_p}\circ\theta_{K[n]}=\theta_K[n]\circ s^n_{P_{p'}P_g}$, where $s^n$ denotes the composite shift comparisons. No cartesian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The universal comparison [def-sfb-left-derived-exact] is leftDerivedUnique. Its factorization identity, evaluated on the homotopy image of any complex, identifies the comparison followed by the termwise factorization of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] with the universal counit. Expand mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh_hom_app and the identity components of quotientCompQhIso and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors. This proves modulePullbackResolutionCounit_eq on every complex. Naturality proves the first resolution equation; shift compatibility from the first step proves the second. Neither equation needs the K-flatness or quasi-isomorphism assumption, so no preservation-of-K-flatness lemma is required.

proof.text: The canonical comparison [def-sfb-left-derived-exact] is definitionally the published leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Expand the compositor [prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp], namely leftDerivedFunctorNatIso followed by leftDerivedFunctorCompIso. Cancel the exact comparison for the intermediate composite. Naturality interchanges the two whiskered comparisons, and inverse cancellation gives the stated exact-normalization equality. For [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp], the component of its termwise map on M[n] in degree r is definitionally its original component on M.X(r+n).

proof.text: Use the published proved instances commShift_mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_hom and commShift_mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_hom from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Shift.ExactFunctor. They descend the degreewise shift equations through the universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], using the shift-compatible factorizations [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Solve the exact-normalization equation of step 4 for the compositor by composing with the inverses of the two whiskered comparisons. Each factor commutes with shifts by step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. Therefore so does their composite, and its inverse by Mathlib of_iso_inv.

proof.text: For the arbitrary commutative square, the two compositors and their inverses commute with shifts by step 5. Equality of composite scheme morphisms induces a shift-compatible identification: substitute the equality, reducing to the identity natural transformation of the same specified derived functor. The square comparison is the composite of these three maps, so [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] applies. Its shift_app_comm component at K and n, reversed, is precisely the claimed equation. No cartesian hypothesis is used.

All 6 steps check out. (1) P_u is exact: det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main makes f^* exact, so lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization applies; the transported shift makes c_u a triangle iso, and TR1 isomorphism-closure gives exactness. (2) G_u is exact by lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated, which is unsplit but Lean-closed. Its Lean (RightDerivedFunctor/Triangulated.lean:94-99) transports the shift from K(Inj), so it is the K-injective shift; the degreewise identification u_*(I[n])=(u_*I)[n] is correct. (3) I recomputed both tensor reindexings against the differential in def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso: identity on V[n]⊗B, sign (-1)^{np} on B⊗V[n]. So shifted K-flat resolutions are valid and F(t[n])=F(t)[n]. (4) q∘m=Q(B)∘e_h type-checks and descends by localization clauses (2)/(3). Since e_u=a_u∘c_uQ=ε_u (def-sfb-left-derived-exact), it is the same equation as step 4 of prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp, so m is that node's compositor and not a free choice. (5) The shift compatibility of e and q follows from factorization clause (2) and the commshift whisker/composition leaf; it reduces to B_{M[n]}=B_M[n], then extends by clause (3). (6) I checked the inverse identity and the θ chain; only gp'=pg' is used, no cartesian hypothesis.
